page.name: SaaS & online services
page.h1: Messaging for SaaS and online services
page.metaTitle: Messaging for SaaS and online services
page.metaDescription: Two-factor codes, onboarding nudges, incident alerts and renewal reminders over the messaging accounts your team already runs.
page.lede: Your login codes, incident notices and renewal nudges sit on the critical path of someone else’s workday. Send them from your own service with a tenant API key, and read the outcome back through the same API.

sections.h: The messages on your users’ critical path
bullets: Security alerts — new device, password change
Incident and maintenance notices to affected accounts

sections.h: Send from your code, not a console
p: Product messaging is generated by your application, not typed by a human. The platform exposes an open API for sending, with per-tenant API keys, so the code that emits the event is the code that sends the message. The console is there for operational sends and for looking at what happened.
bullets: Send from your own service with a tenant API key
Read message status back through the API — acceptance, and the delivery status wherever the provider reports it
Push receipt events to your own endpoint instead of polling

p: Which of your users may be messaged, how often, and what a message is allowed to say — that is your product decision. On the SMS channel the platform applies the routing, pacing and suppression rules you configure; it does not decide your notification policy.

faq.q: Can I send the same code from two services without duplicating it?
faq.a: Not automatically. The send API has no idempotency key, so a retried call produces a second message. Duplicate suppression has to live in the caller.

faq.q: Do you retry a failed send for me?
faq.a: Retry behavior is explicit rather than automatic: a failed message records its error code, and re-sending is a decision your service makes. Scheduling and bulk behavior are documented in the help center.

faq.q: Can receipts be pushed to our own webhook?
faq.a: Yes — the platform can push delivery receipt events to an endpoint you configure. The reliability caveats for callbacks are covered in the guides.
